extracted.intended_audience: K-12 schools and libraries, service providers, program administrators (USAC), and stakeholders/commenters on the FCC Schools and Libraries Cybersecurity Pilot Program
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and proposed requirements for a three-year FCC pilot program providing USF funding for cybersecurity and advanced firewall services for eligible K-12 schools and libraries, including application content, reporting, audits, funding rules, and administrator responsibilities. The document also solicits comments on metrics, budget, duration, and program design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal — Improve security and protection of E-Rate-funded networks and data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission proposes a program goal of improving the security and protection of E-Rate-funded broadband networks and data for participating K-12 schools and libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Pilot funding may help participants acquire cybersecurity and advanced firewall services and equipment needed to improve security. The Commission seeks comment on how to measure whether the Pilot is effective in protecting and securing networks and data and on this goal and related questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal — Measure costs and effectiveness of funded services/equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission proposes a goal of measuring the costs and effectiveness of cybersecurity and advanced firewall services and equipment purchased with Pilot funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Pilot should gather data on the types of services and equipment purchased and associated cost and effectiveness. Data from Pilot equivalents of FCC Forms 470/471 can be used. The Commission asks what data should be collected on effectiveness, and whether requirements should be standardized across participants for comparative analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal — Evaluate leveraging of other federal K-12 cybersecurity resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission proposes evaluating how best to leverage free and low-cost federal K-12 cybersecurity tools and resources (e.g., CISA, DOE, NIST) to help schools and libraries address cybersecurity needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission asks whether the Pilot should require participants to implement some or all of CISA's 'highest priority steps' (e.g., multi-factor authentication, patching known flaws, backups, incident response plans, training) and how to incentivize use of federal resources and USAC's training/distribution relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics/data to collect from Pilot participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested metrics the Commission could require Pilot participants to collect and submit to measure effectiveness and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed: number of intrusion attempts; number of successful attacks; mean time to detection and response; estimated cost of each attack; number and percent of users employing multi-factor authentication; frequency of staff/student cyber training sessions and participation rates; awareness/readiness assessments based on CISA or other guidance. The Commission asks what other accepted metrics should be required and whether requirements should be standardized for comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum information the Commission proposes Pilot applications must include to apply to be a Pilot participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a minimum: (i) name, address, contact info (and listing of all schools/libraries for district/system applicants); (ii) description of current cybersecurity posture and proposed advanced cybersecurity action plan; (iii) description of any unauthorized operational access incidents within one year (date range, description, impact, vulnerabilities exploited, techniques used, actor identifiers if known); (iv) description of proposed use of funding, types of services/equipment to purchase, and implementation plan; (v) description of how participant will collect and track progress and provide required Pilot data and how funding impacted pre-existing cybersecurity plans. Applications proposed to be submitted via USAC online platform; the Commission seeks comment on confidentiality/security protections for this information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant eligibility (entities eligible to apply)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities proposed as respondents/participants in the Pilot program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document language indicates respondents: state, local or tribal government institutions, and other not-for-profit institutions; generally framed for eligible K-12 schools and libraries. Service providers will also participate for reimbursement processes. The Commission seeks comment on eligibility and selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot structure — selection, funding commitments, reimbursement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed structure for how the Pilot will operate from application to funding to reimbursement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested schools and libraries apply to be participants; selected participants apply for funding for Pilot-eligible services and equipment; participants receiving funding commitments may begin receiving services/equipment and submit invoices for reimbursement. The Commission proposes USAC be the permanent administrator and seeks comment on this structure; the Bureau would review applications and select participants in consultation with other FCC offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed length of the Pilot program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission proposes a three-year term for funding availability and asks whether three years is sufficient to evaluate effectiveness, whether ramp-up or close-out time should be included, and whether shorter alternatives (e.g., single application window until funds exhausted) might be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot budget and overall funding amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed total budget for the Pilot program and questions on sufficiency and distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission proposes $200 million over three years. It asks whether $200 million is sufficient to obtain meaningful data, whether a lower budget (e.g., $100M) could suffice, how to distribute the budget across years, and forecasting issues if participants access larger amounts earlier in the term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding caps and per-recipient limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations for setting maximum awards and caps to participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission asks whether to establish a maximum funding cap per participant; a per-student cap (and library caps based on square footage) based on commercially available costs; data sources for cost information; whether to adjust awards based on category two discount rate levels; or allow individualized award amounts. The Commission also asks whether participants should be required to contribute a portion of costs and how to ensure cost-effective purchases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding distribution strategy (many small awards vs few large awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to disburse smaller amounts to more participants or larger amounts to fewer participants and the tradeoffs for data collection and program insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission asks which approach would generate better data: broader coverage for more cybersecurity data or deeper funding for holistic case studies. The question ties to program goals of obtaining meaningful and actionable data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-share / non-discount share requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: How participants' non-discount share of costs should be determined and whether participants must contribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission proposes that Pilot participants be subject to their current category two discount rate as the non-discounted share, but asks whether instead participants should contribute a fixed percentage of costs. It seeks comment on whether the service provider's non-discount share should be waived and how to ensure participants make cost-effective purchases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to leverage free/low-cost federal resources and implement CISA recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how the Pilot should require or incentivize participants to use federal cybersecurity resources and implement CISA's recommended 'highest priority steps.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of CISA's recommendations include implementing a small number of highest priority steps such as multi-factor authentication, fixing known cybersecurity flaws, performing/backing up and testing backups, minimizing exposure to common attacks, developing/exercising incident response plans, and training/awareness campaigns. The Commission asks whether the Pilot should require a certain number of these steps be implemented to receive funding, and how to enforce such requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements — annual progress and final reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed reporting obligations for Pilot participants during and after the Pilot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission proposes participants submit information to apply, a progress report for each year, and a final report at conclusion. Reports should include how Pilot funding was used, changes or advancements outside of Pilot-funded services, number of cyber incidents each year and whether the participant successfully defended its network/data, and other data to evaluate effectiveness. The Commission seeks comment on additional assessments participants should conduct and what data to collect for comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measurement and standardization for comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: Need to define goals and objective criteria and consider standardization across participants to compare outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission emphasizes defining performance goals and asks how best to measure progress towards goals (objective criteria for improved protection/security), what information to collect to compare Pilot results, whether to standardize some requirements across participants to allow comparative analysis, and which outcomes to measure (reductions in attacks, average cost of attack, time to detect/respond, staff/user awareness/readiness, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must disclose specified recent cybersecurity incidents as part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should include a description of any incident of unauthorized operational access within a year of application date, with date ranges, descriptions of unauthorized access, impact, vulnerabilities exploited, techniques used, and identifying information for actors if known. This information is intended to inform selection and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invoice and reimbursement documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Required documentation and procedures for requesting reimbursement from the Pilot program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Along with completed FCC Form 472 (applicant reimbursement) or FCC Form 474 (service provider reimbursement), applicants/service providers must submit invoices detailing items purchased. The Administrator shall accept and review requests for reimbursement and invoices subject to invoice filing deadlines. Service providers must include specific certifications on Form 474 (see certifications entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invoice filing deadline and extension policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines for submitting invoices for reimbursement and permissible extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invoices must be submitted within ninety (90) days after the last date to receive service, per §54.2001. Billed entities or service providers may request one one-time ninety (90) day extension of the invoice filing deadline if timely filed; the Administrator shall grant such an extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audits, inspections, and investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit and inspection rights and participant obligations for compliance evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants shall be subject to audits and other investigations to evaluate compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements, including what services/equipment were purchased, delivered, and used. Participants shall permit any representative (including auditors) appointed by state education departments, the Administrator, the Commission and its Office of Inspector General, or other agencies with jurisdiction to enter premises to conduct inspections for compliance. Audits will be conducted in accordance with generally accepted government auditing standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records retention and production requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordkeeping obligations and production duties for Pilot participants and applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants shall retain all documents related to participation sufficient to demonstrate compliance with program rules for at least 10 years from the last date of service or equipment delivery. Applicants must maintain asset and inventory records sufficient to verify actual location of services/equipment for 10 years after purchase. Participants must present records upon request by authorized representatives or auditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service provider and applicant certification and attestation statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Required certifications and penalty-of-perjury attestations to be included on FCC Forms (e.g., Forms 472, 474) by applicants and service providers seeking reimbursement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: an authorized person must certify under penalty of perjury that submitted data is true, accurate, and complete; compliance with program rules and acknowledgement that failure to comply may result in denial, cancellation, recoupment, civil/criminal penalties; expenditures are for authorized purposes; service provider not seeking duplicate reimbursement; non-discount portion not waived by service provider; submission of invoices with requests; compliance with gift rules; acknowledgment of audits and records retention for ten years; no kickbacks; not debarred or suspended; no use of funds to purchase or maintain equipment/services from companies designated as national security threats; compliance with §54.10 regarding covered communications equipment/services. False statements may be punished under federal statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator responsibilities, authority limits, and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Roles and duties of the Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC) as the permanent Administrator of the Pilot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USAC shall review applications, recommend funding commitments, issue funding commitment decision letters, review invoices and recommend payment, create and maintain a website posting applications for services, provide the Commission full access to collected data, provide performance measurements upon request, audit entities reporting data, and establish procedures to verify support amounts. The Administrator may not make policy or interpret statutes/rules and must seek Commission guidance where unclear. If the Administrator's participation ends, it must make available free of charge any and all intellectual property generated in administering the program and be subject to close-out audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of support amounts and suspension/delay of payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrator authority to verify support amounts and suspend or delay disbursements when verification is inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator shall establish procedures to verify support amounts and may suspend or delay support amounts if a party fails to provide adequate verification of support amounts upon reasonable request from the Administrator or the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals, requests for review, and waiver procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures, timelines, and content requirements for parties seeking review of Administrator decisions or waivers of Commission rules under the Pilot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any party aggrieved by an Administrator action must first seek review from the Administrator; may then seek review from the FCC. Parties seeking waivers of the Commission's rules in this subpart shall seek relief directly from the Commission and need not first seek Administrator review. Filing deadlines: 30 days to file a request for review of Administrator decision; 30 days to file a request for review to the Commission after Administrator decision. Requests must contain party interest, full statement of material facts with supporting affidavits/docs, question presented with references to rules/orders/statutes, statement of relief sought and statutory/regulatory basis; must serve copies on the Administrator and any third parties alleged to have engaged in prohibitive conduct. The Wireline Competition Bureau conducts de novo review of Administrator decisions, and the Commission conducts de novo review of decisions raising novel questions of fact, law, or policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited equipment and national security compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on use of universal service support to obtain or maintain equipment/services from companies designated as national security threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifications require that no universal service support has been or will be used to purchase, obtain, maintain, improve, modify, or otherwise support any equipment or services produced or provided by any company designated by the FCC as posing a national security threat to communications networks or the communications supply chain since effective date of designations. Also references compliance with §54.10 and prohibition on using federal subsidies to obtain covered communications equipment/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards by which audits of Pilot participants and reported data shall be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Commission, the Administrator, or any independent auditor conducts audits of participants, such audits shall be conducted in accordance with generally accepted government auditing standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset and inventory record requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to maintain asset and inventory records sufficient to verify location of purchased services and equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applicants shall maintain asset and inventory records of services and equipment purchased sufficient to verify the actual location of such services and equipment for a period of 10 years after purchase; these records must be presented upon request by authorized representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and transparency of comments and submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of comments, reply comments, and ex parte submissions and the public posting of Pilot-related documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments and related submissions will be publicly available online via ECFS. The Commission provides links to the official PDF and metadata; public inspection copy is available. The document solicits public comments by specified dates on the NPRM and PRA information collection requirements.
